## Conclusion 2

**Aurora kinase inhibitors** (stated probability 0.55); key evidence e15, e4, e8, e2, e9.

Why: Two independent morphology calls favour Aurora cytokinesis failure with frequent bilobed/binucleate nuclei; weak low-similarity NSC kept as alternative.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Phospho-histone H3 plus ploidy flow cytometry and live imaging of mitosis to test cytokinesis failure/polyploidy versus DNA-break signalling.

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Top call not justified over runner-up. NSC is 3/4 for DNA damage but with low similarities (0.49-0.61) and DNA replication also present, while the only direct morphology call favours Aurora kinase inhibitors: enlarged/binucleate-bilobed nuclei, increased integrated DNA, enlarged spread cells, preserved tubulin/actin. Large-nucleus/cell-area effects (z +17 to +31) are consistent across 0.3-10 uM and explainable by both hypotheses; the discriminating binucleation signal is strongest at 0.3 uM (frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+5.98) and falls with dose, yet phenotype was described only at 1 and 10 uM. Probability 0.5 for DNA damage is therefore over-calibrated.

Requested: Free describe_phenotype (no new acquisition) on already-acquired well w_6165ed4a04, dose index 3 (0.3 uM, replicate 1), scoring binucleate/bilobed nuclei in a shared cytoplasm versus predominantly single enlarged nuclei. Frequent binucleation supports Aurora kinase inhibitors/cytokinesis failure; single enlarged nuclei without binucleation supports DNA damage.

Compound: **AZ-A** (no PubChem record shown)

Identity check: BBBC021 gives no structure for this compound (an internal code); name matches in PubChem would be unrelated compounds, so none is shown

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Aurora kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

Early quantitative signals were right about the biology but wrong about the class. Wells at 0.3-10 uM (e2, e3, e7, e8) all showed extreme frac_large_nucleus z +24 to +31 with cell_area and nuc_area z +17 to +29, plus lower density, which fits Aurora-linked polyploid enlargement (PMID 37881124) and Aurora inhibition-induced polyploidy (PMID 38875929). The two microscopist calls (e4, e15) correctly flagged this as Aurora-like enlarged/binucleate-bilobed nuclei with preserved tubulin/actin.

What was right:
- Microscopist describe_phenotype in e4 and e15 correctly prioritized enlarged/binucleate-bilobed nuclei and spread cells as Aurora/cytokinesis-failure-like over DNA damage.
- Quantitative large-nucleus and cell/nuclear area signals (z +17 to +31 in e2, e3, e7, e8) correctly captured a saturated polyploid enlargement phenotype present even at 0.3 uM.
- Dose-response e10-e12 correctly showed saturated frac_large_nucleus (rho -0.20) with falling cell count (rho -1.00) and strongest multinucleate proxy at low dose, pointing to polyploidization rather than dose-escalating toxicity alone.

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-weighted compare_to_reference_atlas NSC 3/4 DNA-damage vote in e9 despite low similarities 0.49-0.61 and competing DNA-replication neighbors in e5/e9, leading to first conclusion DNA damage p=0.50 in e14.
- Acquisition choice to describe_phenotype only at 1 and 10 uM (e4) while the discriminating binucleation signal was strongest at 0.3 uM (frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+5.98), missing the key Aurora vs single-enlarged-nucleus distinction until the review-requested e15.
- First hypothesis update e13 treated NSC majority as prior over direct morphology, over-calibrating DNA damage; correction required the free re-description of w_6165ed4a04 at 0.3 uM.

Proposed next experiment: Phospho-histone H3 Ser10 immunofluorescence plus DNA-content flow cytometry and short live imaging of mitosis to test Aurora-like cytokinesis failure and polyploidization versus DNA-break signaling.
